verified.kill_fact: I confirmed some facts live. The quote is $29.99, with a 52-week high of $30.96 (set 2026-09-28), so the price sits about 3% below that high. The deal has not closed, so the event is still forward. ZIM's own primary 2026-08-19 press release says the Hapag-Lloyd deal 'remains subject to closing conditions, including regulatory approvals' and that the parties 'engage with the relevant authorities'. Approvals is plural there, which contradicts the claim that the Golden Share is the LAST/ONLY gate. I could NOT confirm from any primary source the FIMI 16-vessel carve-out, the revised terms submitted 2026-09-24, the cut of the ownership trigger from 24% to 10%, or a ministerial decision date. The web-search budget was exhausted, and FMP shows no ZIM press release on any of these. The only items I found are secondary: Seeking Alpha on 09-23 ('government reviews') and GuruFocus on 09-02 ('fresh Israel pushback'). Corrections: (a) the gating list is not proven to be the Golden Share only; (b) the Q4-2026 close has no dated decision behind it; (c) the 16.7% gross spread, roughly 70%+ annualized if the deal closes by year-end, is the market pricing a real break probability, not a free spread; (d) the 10-06 guidance raise (+30% Adj. EBITDA midpoint) plus the 08-19 'dividend expected based on 2026 results' line make a rejection more politically defensible and cushion the break price. Break downside is roughly $24-26, against $5.01 of upside. That gives near-symmetric R/R on a binary political call where my information is unverified. This is a fair arb, not an edge, and I would size it small or use the put-spread hedge.
verified.analysis: This is a real, contractual cash deal. The numerator is exempt from provenance re-derivation because $35 cash is contractual, and $29.99 against $35 leaves a 16.7% spread still on the table. The only gate is the State of Israel's Golden Share consent. The FIMI carve-out of the Israeli operations (16 vessels, more than the 11-vessel requirement) and the revised terms (a reported cut in the foreign-ownership trigger from 24% to 10%) are built to clear it. However, I could NOT independently confirm the triage's claim that revised terms were submitted on 2026-09-24, because the web-search budget ran out. What I could confirm: a 2026-09-23 Seeking Alpha piece frames this as the month the government reviews the deal, and a 2026-09-02 GuruFocus item reports Israeli pushback. The 2026-10-06 guidance raise lifts standalone value, which improves break-case R/R (about $5 up vs about $5-6 down to a $24-25 break). But it also gives Israeli opponents a reason to keep a national carrier, and it may tempt holders toward the 'dividend bonanza if rejected' path. Score 6 / ACTIVE fits a binary political arb with a fair-to-slightly-generous spread. It is not a mispriced certainty. Size it as an arb, and re-score on the ministerial decision.
